content.text: No Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or early-termination charges exist anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, minimum-fee or early-termination charge on Sparkling, so it sits at our preferred position. Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule (p0084); Sparkling's convenience termination right on 90 days' notice (Section 17(b), p0118) carries no exit fee or accelerated fees, and termination for Garman's default converts the licence to perpetual with no further fees plus a refund of prepaid fees for services not rendered (p0128). Section 8 likewise requires Garman, not Sparkling, to repay amounts on rejection. The only monetary exposure identified for Sparkling is chargeable repair services at Fee Schedule rates for Sparkling-caused faults (p0077), which is a service charge rather than a liquidated amount or penalty. No redline required.
